questions.question: State the quadrant of each point and describe how to plot it: (3; 2), (−2; 4), (−3; −1), (4; −2).
questions.expected_answer: (3; 2): 3 right, 2 up, quadrant one (x positive, y positive). (−2; 4): 2 left, 4 up, quadrant two (x negative, y positive). (−3; −1): 3 left, 1 down, quadrant three (both negative). (4; −2): 4 right, 2 down, quadrant four (x positive, y negative). The horizontal move for x always comes first.

questions.question: A bath is filled steadily for 10 minutes, someone sits in it for 20 minutes, and it drains in 5 minutes. Describe the global graph of volume against time you would sketch, including axis labels and the relative steepness of the sections.
questions.expected_answer: Horizontal axis: time in minutes, marked 10, 30 and 35. Vertical axis: volume in litres. From 0 to 10 minutes a straight line increasing from the origin; from 10 to 30 minutes a horizontal (constant) section; from 30 to 35 minutes a straight line decreasing to zero. The draining section is steeper than the filling section because the same volume leaves in half the time.

questions.question: Explain how you decide whether to join plotted points with a ruler, a smooth curve, or not at all, giving an example of each.
questions.expected_answer: Plot all points first. If the independent variable is continuous and the points line up (constant difference), use a ruler: y = 2x + 1. If the independent variable is continuous and the points bend, draw a smooth freehand curve: y = x^2 − 1, a U with its lowest point at (0; −1); a ruler would make a wrong pointed V. If the independent variable is discrete, such as passengers at R15 each, leave the dots unjoined.
